issues.legal_issue: An application to recover possession under a special agricultural debt relief scheme is not barred by limitation when that scheme prescribes no limitation period for recovery of possession.
material_facts: The debt and the charge over the agricultural land were governed by a special statutory scheme under which the award could be executed as an order of a civil court.
The debt was discharged through a compromise, but the mortgagee’s successors remained in possession.
The mortgagor’s successors applied under the scheme to recover possession, and the scheme prescribed no limitation period for such an application.
The challengers relied on the passage of time and the limitation period for executing a decree.
issues.conclusion: The application for possession was not barred by limitation; the limitation period applicable to suits for possession did not apply to the application under the scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3 and 27 of the Limitation Act, 1963, a right to property is extinguished only when a prescribed period for instituting a suit for possession expires; section 27 concerns a suit whose limitation period is prescribed in the Act’s Schedule. Section 29(2) applies where a special or local law prescribes a different limitation period. The special scheme, including sections 32(2)(v), 38(3), 46 and 51A, provided for recovery through an application and prescribed no limitation period for recovery of possession. Section 51A restricted civil-court jurisdiction, so a person seeking possession under the scheme was not required to institute an ordinary suit for possession. Article 136 could govern recovery of money under an award but did not govern an application to recover possession under the scheme. The contrary part of Ramanbhai Trikamlal v. Vaghri Vaghabhai Oghabhai was overruled; Madhav Laxman Vaikunthe v. State of Mysore was referred to in distinguishing claims to recover money.

predicates.application_for_possession_under_special: The person entitled to possession applied to recover it through a special statutory scheme.
predicates.scheme_prescribes_no_possession_limitati: The scheme governing the application prescribed no limitation period for recovering possession.
predicates.ordinary_suit_for_possession: The person seeking possession was required to bring an ordinary suit for possession.

issues.definition: When a person applies for possession through a special scheme that sets no limitation period for that application and does not require an ordinary possession suit, the application is not barred by limitation.

issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee’s continued possession does not become adverse possession without proof that a hostile title was asserted to the owner’s knowledge.
material_facts: The mortgagee’s successors remained in possession after the debt was discharged.
There was no evidence showing when they asserted a title hostile to the mortgagor’s successors or that the latter knew of and acquiesced in such an assertion.
The mortgagor’s successors applied to recover possession under the special scheme.
issues.conclusion: The mortgagee’s successors did not establish title by adverse possession.
issues.legal_principle: A possession-based claim to ownership requires proof that the possessor asserted a hostile title to the owner’s knowledge. Mere continued possession, including possession that began as mortgagee possession, does not establish adverse possession without that proof. The court also held that no limitation period was prescribed under the scheme for an application to recover possession.

predicates.application_for_possession_under_special: The person entitled to possession applied to recover it through a special statutory scheme.
predicates.possession_began_as_mortgagee: The possessor entered or continued in possession in the capacity of a mortgagee.
predicates.no_hostile_title_known_to_owner_proved: The claimant did not prove that a hostile title was asserted and brought to the owner’s knowledge.

issues.definition: In an application for possession under a special scheme, a person who possessed as mortgagee does not establish title by adverse possession when no hostile title known to the owner is proved.

issues.legal_issue: A claimed purchase at a public auction does not establish ownership when the claimant fails to produce the records that would substantiate the sale and the available payment evidence is inconclusive.
material_facts: The mortgagee’s successors claimed that the land had been sold by a public authority to recover dues and that the mortgagee had purchased it.
Payment receipts showed deposits, but did not establish that the payments were made as the purchase price for the land or pursuant to an auction.

The claimants did not produce the sale notification, sale proceedings or sale certificate, although those documents would have been expected if the sale had occurred under the applicable recovery procedure.
The challengers appealed from an order requiring delivery of possession.
issues.conclusion: The claimed auction purchase was not established, an adverse inference was justified, and the mortgagee’s successors remained mortgagees rather than owners.
issues.legal_principle: When a sale for recovery of dues is claimed, the required recovery procedure and its records, including the sale certificate, provide the best evidence of the sale. Withholding material evidence that would establish the sale justifies an adverse inference against the party relying on it. A mortgagee remains a mortgagee unless a valid basis for a change in the character of possession is established; while the debt remains unpaid, the property remains subject to the charge.

rule.if: appeal_against_possession_order and ownership_claimed_through_public_auction and key_sale_records_not_produced and payment_evidence_inconclusive

predicates.appeal_against_possession_order: A party appealed from an order requiring delivery of possession.
predicates.ownership_claimed_through_public_auction: The party resisting delivery claimed ownership through a public auction sale.
predicates.key_sale_records_not_produced: The party claiming the sale did not produce the records that would substantiate its authorization and completion.
predicates.payment_evidence_inconclusive: The available payment evidence did not establish that the payments were made as the purchase price for the property or pursuant to its auction.

issues.definition: On an appeal from a possession order, a claimed auction purchase does not establish ownership when the key sale records are withheld and the payment evidence is inconclusive.

issues.legal_issue: A court executing an award for delivery of possession may award mesne profits as a consequence of ordering possession when the former mortgagee retains and enjoys the property after discharge of the debt.
material_facts: The mortgagee’s successors continued to possess and enjoy the land after the mortgagor discharged the debt.
The charge created by the award ended when the debt was paid, after which the mortgagor’s successors became entitled to possession and mesne profits.
The civil court found that the land generated income at the rate used to assess mesne profits, and no contrary material was produced.
The civil court ordered delivery of possession and awarded mesne profits for the period preceding the application through delivery of possession.
issues.conclusion: The executing court had power to award mesne profits as an incident of its order for delivery of possession, and the award was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under the scheme’s execution provisions, including sections 38(3) and 46, the award was executed as an order of the civil court and the Code of Civil Procedure applied to proceedings under the relevant chapter. Mesne profits arising from unlawful retention of possession after discharge of the debt are consequential to execution of the possession award and may be ordered as an incident of delivery of possession.

rule.if: execution_for_delivery_of_possession and debt_discharged and former_mortgagee_retained_and_enjoyed_property and court_found_property_income

predicates.execution_for_delivery_of_possession: A party sought execution of an award requiring delivery of possession.
predicates.debt_discharged: The debt secured by the property had been paid or otherwise discharged.
predicates.former_mortgagee_retained_and_enjoyed_pr: The former mortgagee continued to possess and enjoy the property after the debt was discharged.
predicates.court_found_property_income: The court found that the property generated income and had no contrary material before it.

issues.definition: When a discharged debt is followed by a former mortgagee’s continued possession and enjoyment of income-producing property, a court executing a possession award may also award mesne profits.
